11.explanation: The walkway is 3 ft wide on all sides. Garden dimensions: Length = 30 − 2(3) = 24 ft, Width = 20 − 2(3) = 14 ft. Perimeter = 2(24 + 14) = 76 ft

12.text: Which set has a domain of {2, 3} and a range of {5, 8}?
12.explanation: Domain is the set of x-values, range is the set of y-values. Option H has domain {2, 3} and range {5, 8}.

13.text: Some students are selling candy bars to raise money to purchase new gym equipment. The more candy bars they sell, the more money they raise. Which of these is the independent variable in this situation?
options: The number of candy bars sold
The cost of new gym equipment
13.explanation: The independent variable is what you control or change. Students control how many candy bars they sell, which then determines the money raised.

14.text:
A line contains the points represented by this table of values.

This line has a y-intercept of —
14.explanation: The pattern shows y = x + 3. When x = 0, y = 3. The y-intercept is 3.

18.text:
What value of p makes this equation true?
2p=−3(p+2)4
18.explanation: Multiply both sides by 4: 8p = −3(p + 2). Expand: 8p = −3p − 6. Add 3p: 11p = −6. Divide by 11: p = −6/11

19.text:
The math club had $200 to buy supplies for t-shirt decorating.
• They spent $10 for the first t-shirt and $8 for each additional t-shirt.
• They purchased y t-shirts.

Which inequality best represents this situation?
19.explanation: First t-shirt costs $10, then (y−1) additional t-shirts at $8 each. Total: 10 + 8(y−1) must be ≤ 200 (cannot exceed budget).

20.text:
Greta has 2 bags of tiles that are all the same size and shape.
• Bag A has 1 blue tile and 3 green tiles.
• Bag B has 2 yellow tiles and 4 black tiles.

Which of these best describes dependent events?
options: Randomly selecting one tile from Bag A, replacing the tile, then randomly selecting another tile from Bag A
Randomly selecting one tile from Bag B, not replacing the tile, then randomly selecting another tile from Bag B
Randomly selecting one tile from Bag A, replacing the tile, then randomly selecting one tile from Bag B
Randomly selecting one tile from Bag B, not replacing the tile, then randomly selecting one tile from Bag A
20.explanation: Dependent events occur when the first event affects the probability of the second. Not replacing the tile from Bag B changes the probability for the second selection.

21.text: A spinner has four equal sections labeled W, X, Y, and Z. A fair coin has faces labeled heads and tails. Edward will spin the arrow of the spinner and flip the coin one time each. What is the probability the arrow will land on the section labeled Z and the coin will land with heads face-up?
21.explanation: P(Z) = 1/4 and P(heads) = 1/2. For independent events: P(Z and heads) = 1/4 × 1/2 = 1/8

22.text:
Stella has some colored cards that are the same size and shape.
• The probability of randomly selecting a blue card is 20%.
• The probability of randomly selecting a red card is 30%.

What is the probability Stella will randomly select a card that is NOT blue, replace it, then randomly select a card that is red?

23.text:
Emma is on the school golf team. Her scores from 15 practice rounds are shown.
93, 95, 102, 107, 107, 108, 111, 113, 114, 114, 115, 118, 120, 120, 125

From the sample scores collected, can you perform a non-biased statistical analysis for the school golf team?
options: Yes, because the golfer is in the school
No, because the scores are only from practice rounds
No, because the scores are only from one member of the golf team
Yes, because the data include scores from a large number of practice rounds
23.explanation: To analyze the entire team, you need data from all team members, not just one golfer. This sample is biased.

24.text:
A baker recorded the number of batches of cookies he made on each of seven days. He baked a different number of batches of cookies each day. This boxplot summarizes his data.

The baker baked 30 batches of cookies on the eighth day. He redraws the boxplot to include the additional data. Which statement comparing the new boxplot to the original boxplot is NOT true?
options: The value of the interquartile range increased.
24.explanation: Adding 30 batches (a high value) increases the upper extreme and median, but does not change the lower extreme (minimum value).

25.text:
The number of points scored by four basketball players during each of 20 games is summarized in these boxplots.

Which player scored 10 or more points in the greatest number of games?
25.explanation: Look at the median and quartiles for each player. Dennis has the highest percentage of games with 10+ points based on the boxplot distribution.

26.text:
The number of points scored by two basketball teams is summarized in these boxplots.

• Team A scored a different number of points in each of the team's 14 games.
• Team B scored a different number of points in each of the team's 13 games.

What is the total number of games in which Team A and Team B each scored 55 or more points?
26.explanation: From the boxplots, count games where each team scored 55+. Team A: about 10 games. Team B: about 8 games. Total: 18 games.

27.text:
A student will collect data about fertilizer and its effect on grass. The student will create a scatterplot to display the amount of fertilizer used and the height of grass after 2 weeks.

To create this scatterplot, the student does NOT need to include —
options: the height of the grass samples
the amount of fertilizer for each sample
the amount of water for each sample
27.explanation: The scatterplot shows fertilizer amount vs. grass height. Water amount is not being plotted, so it's not needed for the scatterplot.

1.text: In paragraph 1, the words "rumbled," "buzzed," and "exploded" evoke images of-
1.explanation: The author uses these active verbs to describe the traffic, lawn mowers, and children playing, creating a vivid sense of the busy energy and movement in the neighborhood.

2.text: The details in paragraph 2 support the idea that Benjamin is -
2.explanation: Benjamin notices the specific details of the sound ("metallic whang," "slightly different note") and immediately decides to investigate its source, demonstrating that he pays attention to his surroundings and is inquisitive.

3.text:
Read this sentence from paragraph 4.
He swung wide around an anonymous heap of metal being swallowed by a greedy mound of blackberry brambles and came to an abrupt halt.
The sentence contains an example of--
3.explanation: The author attributes human characteristics to the blackberry brambles by describing them as "greedy" and saying they are "swallowing" the metal, which is the definition of personification.

4.text:
In this excerpt from paragraph 7, select the words that best reveal Benjamin's attempt to gain the artist's trust.
Craning his head to the side to get another peek at it, he answered politely enough, "My name's Benjamin, and I live up on Hendricks Avenue," waving his hand vaguely at the steep hill behind him. ... Then Benjamin blushed and apologized.
4.explanation: The words "politely" and "apologized" show that Benjamin is being respectful and trying to make amends for his clumsy entrance, hoping to smooth things over with the artist.

5.text: Which situation in the selection is an example of irony?
options: Benjamin is able to discern an artist's noise over all of the other noises he hears.
The artist initially appears hostile to Benjamin but warms to his presence.
The artist is amused by Benjamin and invites him to return the next day to observe the progress on her work.
Benjamin thinks of his neighborhood as quiet only to learn that an artist is noisily constructing a piece of art nearby.
5.explanation: Irony involves a contrast between expectation and reality. Benjamin complains about his "tranquil" neighborhood having nothing to do, only to discover someone creating loud, complex industrial art right down the street.

6.text: According to paragraph 3, the main difference between Super Stadiums and regular stadiums is that Super Stadiums -
6.explanation: Paragraph 3 explains that while Super Stadiums hold a similar number of people as regular stadiums, they offer "additional accommodations, such as restaurants, luxury lounges—even land bridges to neighboring hotels."

7.text: In paragraph 6, which word best describes the author's attitude about Super Stadium projects?
7.explanation: The author warns that the costs are "astronomical" and quotes a source suggesting the goal is to "raise ticket prices," indicating a cautionary attitude regarding the financial impact on fans.

8.text: According to paragraph 7, in the future, sports fans will-
8.explanation: The paragraph explicitly quotes Tom Van Riper, who states that the formula for these stadiums ends with the owners turning around and "rais[ing] ticket prices."

9.text: Which sentence from this selection would be most difficult to verify as a fact?
options: In places with harsh winters, late-season football games can become rather chilly for players and fans alike.
However, inventive architects have always welcomed the opportunity to face such challenges throughout history.
The stadium in Phoenix where the Arizona Cardinals football team plays can be open to the elements on comfortable days or closed to the blazing Arizona sun when the need arises.
Futuristic Super Stadiums dedicated to soccer and rugby are opening in Lyon, France, and Dublin, Ireland.
9.explanation: Statements about what architects have "always welcomed" throughout all of "history" are subjective generalizations that are difficult to prove, unlike specific facts about weather, building features, or locations.

10.text: Based on the selection, the reader may best infer that new building materials -
options: reflect a desire to conserve energy
are sturdy enough to use on any building project
are responsible for yielding more attractive buildings
10.explanation: Paragraph 5 mentions that stadiums use "energy-saving materials," such as a skin designed to reflect the sun and keep the inside cool, showing a focus on conservation.

11.text: Which information about the selection would be best to include in a report about the popularity of spectator sports?
options: The Arizona Cardinals, which are part of the National Football League, play in a new state-of-the-art stadium.
Most stadiums can accommodate 20,000 to 50,000 fans, and some Super Stadiums can hold even more than that.
The new stadium for the New York Giants and Jets cost $1.5 billion.
Sports team owners hope Super Stadiums will bring in more revenue, which can be used to improve team performance.
11.explanation: The fact that stadiums are built to hold massive crowds of 20,000 to 50,000 people (or more) provides concrete evidence of how popular these sports are.

12.text: The purpose of this selection is to--
options: explain how to improve a traditional stadium
entertain the reader with facts about sporting events
persuade the reader to watch live sporting events
describe a popular trend in stadium construction
12.explanation: The entire article focuses on defining "Super Stadiums," detailing their features and costs, and providing examples of this new trend in construction from around the world.

13.text: The purpose of the first paragraph is to -
options: describe one of Osamu Tezuka's drawings
give a preview of Osamu Tezuka's newest manga book
provide a description of Osamu Tezuka's movie scenes
show how Osamu Tezuka's manga differs from older manga
13.explanation: The paragraph uses vivid imagery (a camera looking down, a canoe flipping) to describe a specific action scene found in a manga by Tezuka, illustrating his cinematic style.

14.text: Which question is answered in paragraph 3?
options: How often would Osamu Tezuka sketch pictures?
When did manga become widely popular?
Who invented the manga art form?
How many siblings did Osamu Tezuka have?
14.explanation: The first sentence of paragraph 3 explicitly states: "Tezuka was born in 1928, the oldest of three children," which answers the question about his siblings.

15.text: Paragraph 4 suggests that Osamu Tezuka -
options: spent most of his career writing comic strips for a children's newspaper
nearly decided upon a career in medicine rather than as a manga artist
decided to publish his works in installments instead of publishing books
deeply regretted taking his mother's advice about becoming a doctor
15.explanation: The text explains that he was a medical student "torn between manga and medicine" and had to consult his mother before finally deciding to devote himself to manga.

16.text:
Read this sentence from paragraph 5.
While Tezuka's manga may stand on the same library shelves as American superhero comic books, Tezuka's manga are to most traditional American comic books what Shakespeare's plays are to soap operas on American television: a similar art form, but with much richer content.
The purpose of the analogy in this sentence is to-
options: illustrate the popular themes of American comic books
point out that the manga story lines are similar to American soap operas
emphasize the literary merit of Osamu Tezuka's manga
argue that comic book superheroes are based on Shakespeare's plays
16.explanation: By comparing Tezuka to Shakespeare (high art) and traditional comics to soap operas, the author highlights the superior depth, complexity, and artistic value of Tezuka’s work.

17.text: The author mainly develops the topic of this selection by -
options: summarizing an artist's career and his contribution to modern manga
providing detailed information for creating and publishing original manga
comparing and contrasting an artist's manga with traditional comic books
stating an opinion of manga and supporting it with examples and quotations
17.explanation: The passage follows Tezuka's life from childhood to death, covering his background, his decision to become an artist, his specific stylistic innovations, and his lasting influence on the medium.

18.text: Which information from the selection supports the thesis that manga has become increasingly popular over time?
options: Japanese manga originally contained a dozen sketches that formed one complete story.
Osamu Tezuka's father possessed a substantial collection of his favorite manga.
Osamu Tezuka's work contains borrowed plots from many literary classics.
Manga currently has its own section in many Japanese newspapers.
18.explanation: Paragraph 6 mentions that manga evolved from small strips in the corner of papers to eventually "earning its own section in many Japanese newspapers," demonstrating its growth in popularity.

19.text: In paragraph 2, the author uses dialogue to -
options: communicate critical aspects of the setting
introduce the fears of the main character
add some humor to a serious situation
19.explanation: During a sad farewell, the mother makes a lighthearted comment about visiting because the aunt has the mah-jong set. This causes them both to laugh, momentarily lightening the serious mood.

20.text:
Read this sentence from paragraph 3.
I watched her play with the top button of her coat and thought about the man I was about to meet, my father, whose face I knew only from a small black-and-white photograph.
This sentence conveys Su-Jen's feelings of -
20.explanation: Su-Jen is thinking about meeting a father she does not actually know and has only seen in a picture, which creates a sense of the unknown and uncertainty.

21.text: In paragraph 3, <u>pensive</u> means -
21.explanation: The text describes the mother as "absorbed in her own world" and barely speaking, which aligns with the definition of being contemplative or deep in thought.

22.text:
Read this sentence from paragraph 5.
He stopped as he drew near, huffing out of breath.
This sentence contains an example of--
22.explanation: The word "huffing" phonetically mimics the sound of the heavy breathing it describes, which is the definition of onomatopoeia.

23.text: The character of Su-Jen is mainly revealed through her--
23.explanation: The story is told in the first person ("I"), and the reader understands Su-Jen primarily through her internal narration, observations of her mother, and her memories.

24.text: Based on the selection, Su-Jen's father may best be described as--
24.explanation: Upon meeting Su-Jen, the father gently lifts her, presses her face to his shoulder, and holds her close, demonstrating physical warmth and affection.

25.text: Later chapters of this selection would most likely describe--
options: Su-Jen's adjustment to her new home
the reunions of other Chinese immigrants
Su-Jen's life in a small Chinese village
the construction of a new restaurant
25.explanation: The excerpt concludes with the family arriving in the dark, snowy town of Irvine to start their life together; the natural continuation would be Su-Jen adapting to this new environment.

26.text:
Which word carries a negative connotation in this sentence?
Patrick's mother is assuming that when her son refrains from fraternizing so much, he will become more accomplished.
26.explanation: While "fraternizing" means associating with others, it is often used in a negative context to imply wasting time or associating with the wrong crowd, contrasting with positive words like "accomplished."

27.text:
Read this sentence.
Ryan was meticulous with his writing assignments, so the papers he turned in for English class received the highest grades for grammar because they never contained mistakes.
As used in this sentence, the word meticulous means--
27.explanation: Because Ryan's papers "never contained mistakes" and received high grades for grammar, "meticulous" must mean he was extremely thorough and careful with details.

28.text: Which fact from a magazine article would be best to include in a report about the literary career of William Faulkner?
options: By the time Faulkner entered eighth grade in 1911, he had begun to show signs of increasing truancy.
Faulkner worked briefly as a clerk at First National Bank, which was owned by his grandfather.
Shortly after entering the University of Mississippi, Faulkner won a $10 poetry prize offered by Professor Calvin S. Brown.
In 1921 Faulkner accepted a job as postmaster at the University of Mississippi post office.
28.explanation: Winning a poetry prize is directly related to Faulkner's development and success as a writer ("literary career"), whereas the other options concern his childhood behavior or non-writing jobs.

29.text:
Read these sentences.
The days following tryouts for the wrestling team were a roller coaster ride for Ian. He had done his best at the tryouts and hoped the coaches would want him to wrestle on the varsity team. He worried over it for hours.
The purpose of the figurative language in these sentences is to suggest that Ian--
options: desperately wanted to be on the varsity team
waited a long time to learn the results of the tryouts
29.explanation: A roller coaster has steep ups and downs. This metaphor describes Ian's fluctuating emotions: feeling "up" (hopeful) and then "down" (worried).

30.text: The information in paragraph 2 supports the idea that Antarctic fish -
30.explanation: Paragraph 2 explains that while freezing temperatures should theoretically make the water uninhabitable, many fish live there, setting up the explanation of how they biologically adapt to the cold.

31.text:
Read these sentences from paragraph 3.
The threadfin pithead, for instance, lives at depths of around 2,000 feet in the cold dark of the Antarctic seas. It is difficult to imagine a more adverse environment.
These sentences suggest that the author--
options: admires the unspoiled beauty of Antarctica
appreciates the kinds of life Antarctica supports
is disappointed that so little is known about Antarctica
is dissatisfied that people wrongly see Antarctica as a lifeless place
31.explanation: By acknowledging the "adverse" (harsh) environment and highlighting the specific fish that manage to live there, the author expresses admiration or appreciation for these resilient life forms.

32.text:
Read this sentence from paragraph 3.
The slender fish spends its days swimming through the honeycombed channels of the icepack hunting krillsmall crustaceans-for its sustenance.
The word sustenance means--
32.explanation: The fish hunts krill (small crustaceans) in order to eat them, so "sustenance" refers to the food or nourishment the fish needs to survive.

33.text: Which statement best expresses the main idea of paragraph 3?
options: Fish that live in Antarctic water are called notothenioids.
Fish in the Antarctic Ocean have specialized coloring to hide from predators.
The features of the bald notothen fish help it dominate Antarctic waters.
Many types of fish thrive in the water around Antarctica.
33.explanation: The paragraph states that Antarctica boasts "more than 120 species" of fish that flourish there, and then provides specific examples (threadfin, bald notothen) to illustrate this variety.

34.text: In paragraph 6, the word salutary means--
34.explanation: The text explains that this protein targets ice crystals and prevents the fish from freezing to death. Since it saves the fish's life, the protein is "beneficial."

35.text: The organizational structure of paragraph 6 is best described as -
35.explanation: Paragraph 6 introduces the specific term "AFGP," explains what the acronym stands for, and details exactly what it is and how it functions, which is the structure of a definition.

36.text: Which section would most likely describe future uses of the protein found in fish that live in below-freezing water?
36.explanation: The section titled "Human Applications" explicitly discusses how the protein could be used for organ transplants, deicing, and preserving frozen foods.

37.text: How can the reader best tell that this is an expository selection?
options: It offers a vivid description of ocean fish.
It presents a series of closely related facts.
It reveals the author's stance on an issue.
It focuses on fish rather than humans.
37.explanation: The text provides specific, factual information about water temperatures, fish species, biological mechanisms (proteins), and scientific research, which is characteristic of expository writing.

38.text: What is the author's most likely purpose for writing this selection?
options: To explain how some fish can survive in challenging conditions
To prove that studying fish can be an economic boon for humans
To establish that McMurdo Station performs an important function
To highlight a certain fish that lives in the waters around Antarctica
38.explanation: The central question of the passage is how fish survive in water that should freeze them, and the text answers this by explaining the specific antifreeze protein they possess.

39.text:
That advice helped keep my situation in perspective; I was polishing my craft, getting experience, and establishing myself as a talented writer.
In this sentence from paragraph 1, the word polishing suggests--
39.explanation: In this context, "polishing" means refining or perfecting something. The narrator is working to improve his writing skills ("craft") through experience.

40.text: Which set of statements provides the best summary of paragraphs 2-5?
options: Jake envies his coworker Wylie, who reviews music and theater performances for the newspaper. He is pleased to learn that he will be given the chance to do Wylie's job for a day.
Jake does not think that the Lifestyles editor of the newspaper where he works even knows his name. To his surprise, she stops by and tells him he will be reviewing a classical concert.
Jake is asked to fill in for a coworker who normally reviews cultural performances for the newspaper. He feels excited until he sees that he will be reviewing classical music aimed at children.

Jake is busy reviewing his day's work when he learns he will also have to review a KidsPop concert that will take place the following afternoon. He feels that he does not know much about classical music.
40.explanation: This summary captures the main plot points: the unexpected assignment to cover for a coworker, Jake's initial excitement about a "real" reporting job, and his subsequent disappointment upon realizing it is a children's concert.

41.text:
Read this sentence from paragraph 5.
The ticket was inscribed with the logo for KidsPop, the symphony orchestra's overt attempt to entice children away from video games and into the world of classical music.
What does the word overt mean?
41.explanation: An "overt" attempt is one that is open and obvious rather than hidden. The symphony is clearly and obviously trying to get children interested in music.

42.text:
A quick scan of Saint-Saën's biography provided little assistance--the information was nearly incomprehensible to a beginner such as myself.
The word incomprehensible from paragraph 6 contains a root word that means to--
42.explanation: The word uses the root "prehend" (related to grasping or understanding). Combined with the negative prefix "in-", "incomprehensible" means impossible to understand.

43.text:
Read this sentence from paragraph 10.
Now came a contrast in tempo--the lumbering sluggishness of giant tortoises, painfully trudging along, step by laborious step.
The author uses sensory language in this sentence in order to--
options: illustrate the boredom felt by some of the audience
indicate the musicians are playing much too slowly
show that the music engages the imagination
suggest that the concert will soon be ending
43.explanation: The narrator describes the music using vivid physical movements of animals (lumbering, trudging), showing how the sounds allow him to visualize the animals in his imagination.

44.text:
The fanfare and flourishes of the finale announced a farewell to our carnival.
Which literary device does Jake use in this sentence from paragraph 13?
44.explanation: The repetition of the initial "f" sound in the words "fanfare," "flourishes," "finale," and "farewell" is an example of alliteration.

45.text: Jake's dismay over having to review a KidsPop concert affects the selection by--
45.explanation: The central tension in the story drives from Jake's internal conflict: he wants to be a serious reporter but is stuck reviewing what he considers a childish event.

46.text: Jake uses extensive animal imagery in the selection to suggest the music's--
46.explanation: Descriptions of cackling hens, hopping kangaroos, and dancing elephants highlight the humorous, whimsical, and playful nature of the musical composition.

47.text: Which detail from the selection supports the concept that Jake is eager to do a good job reviewing the concert?
options: He attends although he is older than the kids.
He is comfortable with the extra workload.
He is ready to take notes about the performance.
He imagines the animals as the music portrays them.
47.explanation: Despite his hesitation about the content of the concert, the fact that he arrives with his notepad and pen ready shows his professional dedication to performing his task well.

48.text: The selection is told from Jakes point of view in order to emphasize his--
48.explanation: The first-person perspective allows the reader to experience Jake's internal shift from skepticism to appreciation as he reacts to the music and the audience around him.

49.text: The author includes the illustration at the top of the selection to--
options: add extra information about related technology
offer a representation of a complicated idea
entertain the reader with a cartoon
49.explanation: The article discusses a complex technological concept involving microcircuitry on a lens. The illustration helps the reader visualize what this futuristic technology looks like.

50.text: The purpose of paragraph 2 is to--
options: introduce an obstacle in the improvement of technology
show the similarities between old and new technology
relate current popular beliefs about technology
question the value of new technology
50.explanation: The paragraph explains the difficulty of shrinking computers while keeping the display visible to the human eye, introducing a specific obstacle developers must overcome.

51.text: The author uses the source in paragraph 5 to--
options: compare the device to other technological advancements
relate a personal story about the creation of the device
respond to widespread criticism of the device
51.explanation: The quote from researcher Babak Parviz ("you would see what the display is generating superimposed on the world") provides a simple summary of how the user experiences the technology.

52.text: The reader may conclude that computerized contact lenses will be most useful to people who--
options: prefer to prepare for weather changes
52.explanation: The text mentions applications such as labeling mountain peaks, identifying landmarks, and finding directions, which are tools specifically useful for people traveling in unfamiliar places.

53.text: Paragraph 8 suggests that in the future, computers will be embedded into contact lenses that--
options: can only be worn for short periods of time
53.explanation: Paragraph 8 explicitly states the researcher's hope that the technology will eventually progress to be imprinted on "corrective or prescribed lenses," which are used to fix vision problems.

54.text: The purpose of this selection is to--
options: persuade the reader to try computerized contact lenses
explain the development of computerized contact lenses
evaluate the benefits of wearing computerized contact lenses
describe the process of manufacturing computerized contact lenses
54.explanation: The article is an informational text designed to explain a new technology, detailing who is developing it, how it works, and its potential applications for the future.

1.text: The photograph in the article helps the reader understand —
options: what makes a cheetah a great hunter
why a cheetah has spots on its fur
how cheetahs are able to make quick turns
how cheetahs are different from other cats
1.explanation: The passage explains that cheetahs have paws "more like a dog's paws" instead of regular cat paws, which shows how they are different from other cats.

2.text: The cheetah's coat is most useful because it —
options: keeps the cheetah cool after a long run
lets the cheetah move with great speed
helps the cheetah hide in the grass
protects the cheetah from the sun
2.explanation: Paragraph 3 states that the cheetah's tan coat with black spots "allows a cheetah to blend in with the tall, brown grass in Africa" so other animals don't see it hiding.

3.text: One reason Kelly finishes in third place is because she —
options: has a better bicycle than Marcus
pays attention to the other riders
3.explanation: Kelly practiced on the Oak Park Trails before the race, while Marcus thought he didn't need to practice. This helped Kelly know the course and avoid getting lost like Marcus did.

4.text: Who is telling this story?
4.explanation: The story uses "he" and "she" to talk about the characters, not "I" or "me." This shows a narrator (someone outside the story) is telling what happened.

5.text: Which sentence best states the theme of the story?
options: It is important to admit mistakes.
It is better to join in with friends than to do an activity alone.
It is helpful to encourage others when trying something for the first time.
It is a good idea to prepare before doing something new.
5.explanation: Marcus lost the race because he didn't practice the course beforehand. At the end, he admits he should have practiced with Kelly, showing that preparation is important.

6.text: Which sentence best states the main idea of paragraph 1?
options: The bald eagle was a popular choice for a symbol.
People in America wanted a symbol for their new country.
Congress disagreed about which symbol to select.
The symbol would remind people that they were a free country.
6.explanation: The paragraph says "Americans wanted a symbol for their country's freedom" after winning the Revolutionary War, which is the main point of the paragraph.

7.text: Which heading best belongs above paragraph 2?
7.explanation: Paragraph 2 discusses the debate between choosing the eagle or the turkey as the national symbol, with Benjamin Franklin preferring the turkey.

8.text: Which question is answered in paragraph 2?
options: Who were the Founding Fathers of the United States?
Why was Benjamin Franklin against choosing the bald eagle?
How many types of birds can be found in North America?
Why did Americans want a symbol for their country?
8.explanation: The paragraph explains that Franklin thought the turkey was better because the eagle was "lazy" and "took food from other animals."

9.text: Which word is an antonym for <u>joined</u> as used in paragraph 4?
9.explanation: An antonym means the opposite. If states "joined" to form one country, then "separated" would mean the opposite - to break apart.

10.text: What does <u>defend</u> mean in paragraph 4?
10.explanation: The paragraph says the arrows show the United States is ready to "defend itself," which means to protect itself from harm or danger.

11.text: The author wrote this article most likely to —
options: explain why Americans need a symbol
show ways to honor the bald eagle
share a part of American history
11.explanation: The article tells the historical story of how the bald eagle became America's national symbol, including the debate and decision-making process.

12.text: Which lines show the conflict in the poem?
12.explanation: Lines 5-8 show the problem: "But hunt as I may / I've got only one shoe-- / And where its mate is / I haven't a clue."

13.text: The resolution in the poem happens as soon as the speaker —
13.explanation: When the speaker looks into the yard, they finally see that Otis the dog has the missing shoe as a chew toy, solving the mystery.

14.text: Which word best describes the speaker throughout the poem?
14.explanation: The speaker searches everywhere frantically and says things like "There's clearly no hope," showing they are worried about the missing shoe.

15.text: Which question is answered in paragraph 2?
options: How often do sea otters hunt?
How do sea otters keep their ears closed?
When are sea otters fully grown?
What do sea otters do when they hunt?
15.explanation: Paragraph 2 explains that when hunting, otters close their nostrils and ears to keep out water and can swim as deep as 200 feet to find food.

16.text: What is the main idea of paragraph 4?
options: A sea otter has fur to keep it warm.
A sea otter is a type of mammal.
16.explanation: The paragraph explains that sea otters don't have blubber like other sea animals, so they use their thick two-layer fur to stay warm in cold ocean water.

17.text:
Read this sentence from paragraph 5.
Whole groups of sea otters may be seen floating together.
Which word is a homophone for seen?
17.explanation: A homophone sounds the same but is spelled differently. "Scene" sounds exactly like "seen" but has different letters and meaning.

18.text: Based on the article, the ocean is a perfect home for the sea otter because the —
options: ocean has everything that the sea otter needs
sea otter has few enemies in the ocean
ocean is deep enough for the sea otter to float
sea otter can easily find kelp in the ocean
18.explanation: The article shows the ocean provides food (fish, crabs, clams), kelp for sleeping, and the right environment for the sea otter's lifestyle.

19.text: Based on the article, sea otters can swim well mainly because their —
19.explanation: Paragraph 2 states "Webbed feet help it swim," explaining that the webbing between their toes helps them move through water.

20.text: Based on the article, a sea otter finds its favorite foods —
20.explanation: Paragraph 3 says "a sea otter gathers food from the bottom of the ocean," which is the ocean floor.

21.text: One purpose of the sea otter's chest is to help the animal —
21.explanation: Paragraph 3 explains that the sea otter uses "its chest as a table" and hits shellfish with rocks on its chest to break them open.

22.text: The author uses headings in the article most likely to —
options: list interesting facts about sea otters
tell what can be learned from each section
put information about sea otters in order
22.explanation: The headings like "Time to Eat," "Thick Fur," and "Nap Time" tell readers what topic each section will explain about sea otters.

23.text: Based on the article, what may happen if a sea otter rests far from seaweed?
options: It may become colder more quickly.
It may wake up in another area.
It may have trouble falling asleep.
23.explanation: Paragraph 5 explains that sea otters wrap kelp around themselves to stop from "floating away" while sleeping, so without it they might drift.

24.text: Bonnie and Steve are proud in the beginning of the poem because they each —
options: used a special fruit to make their drinks
believe their drinks are the best
learned how to make new drinks
set up a stand to sell drinks
24.explanation: Bonnie yells "My lemonade's the best" and Steve responds "That's what you think!" showing they both believe their own drink is better.

25.text: Based on the poem, how does Bonnie first find out Steve is selling cherry juice?
options: A boy tells her he bought some.
Steve sets up his stand across the street.
More people are waiting in line at the other stand.
25.explanation: In lines 3-4, a boy walking past tells Bonnie "I just bought some cherry juice!" and tells her to "Go try a glass!"

26.text: Which question is answered in the poem?
options: How do Steve and Bonnie decide to sell cherry lemonade?
How many people bought cherry juice?
Why do Steve and Bonnie decide to have drink stands?
Why is selling drinks a good idea?
26.explanation: The poem shows Bonnie suggesting "Let's mix our drinks together!" and they combine their lemonade and cherry juice to make cherry lemonade.

27.text: Which line from the poem is where the reader understands how the problem is solved?
27.explanation: Line 15 says "Let's mix our drinks together!" which is when Bonnie suggests the solution to their competition problem.

28.text: How is Bonnie different from Steve?
options: She is better at selling drinks.
She is excited about working with someone.
28.explanation: Bonnie is the one who comes up with the idea to combine their drinks and work together, while Steve just agrees with her plan.

29.text: Bonnie and Steve end up sharing a stand because they —
options: are tired of shouting at each other
think they should help each other
become friends after spending time together
want to sell to as many people as possible
29.explanation: Bonnie says "There is a way to reach them all," showing they want to attract more customers by combining their drinks into something everyone will want.

1.text: Another good title for this story would be--
1.explanation: The story is about both Danielle making cupcakes as a surprise for her siblings and her siblings making an apron as a surprise for her. Everyone in the story gives and receives gifts.

2.text: Danielle keeps the cupcakes a secret by--
options: moving them to the laundry room
2.explanation: The passage states that Danielle "had baked cupcakes early in the morning, while Martin and Madison were still asleep," which kept them secret.

3.text: Complete this flow chart with the most appropriate answer for the empty box.
options: Danielle looks at the edges of the apron.
Danielle finds bits of cloth in the laundry room.
Danielle sets the cupcakes on the table.
3.explanation: After receiving the apron and saying "Thank you. It's perfect," the passage says "As she put on the apron, Danielle suddenly remembered the cupcakes she left on the table."

4.text: Danielle is pleased with the surprise most likely because she--
options: needs to wear it when making cupcakes
can cook more often for her family
enjoys wearing blue and yellow clothes
can tell that her family cares about her
4.explanation: Madison says "We wanted to make a surprise for you because you're such a nice sister. You are always thinking of us." This shows her family's care and appreciation for her.

5.text: What will Martin and Madison most likely do next?
5.explanation: At the end, Danielle says "I have a surprise for you too!" and leads them to the kitchen where she left cupcakes for them.

6.text: Which of these do the characters have in common?
6.explanation: All three characters make surprises for each other: Danielle bakes cupcakes for her siblings, and Martin and Madison make an apron for Danielle, showing they all think of others.

7.text: What is the root word in "discovered"?
7.explanation: The root word in "discovered" is "cover." The prefix "dis-" means "not" and the suffix "-ed" shows past tense, so "discovered" means "uncovered" or "found."

8.text: Some people eat seaweed all by itself because they most likely--
options: do not know it is used in other foods
eat many foods that come from the ocean
enjoy foods that add color to the meals they eat
do not like how it tastes mixed with other foods
8.explanation: The passage states that "In some parts of the world, especially near the ocean, people eat seaweed all by itself," suggesting people near oceans commonly eat foods from the sea.

9.text: Based on the article, seaweed makes ice cream and yogurt--
9.explanation: The passage explains that "Without seaweed, ice cream and yogurt would not be as thick or creamy but would seem rather lumpy and watery," showing seaweed affects how they look and their texture.

10.text: Which question is answered in the article?
options: Which ocean has the most seaweed?
Which goods have seaweed in them?
10.explanation: The article mentions several goods that contain seaweed: toothpaste, shampoo, makeup, ice cream, and yogurt. It also states "Hundreds of everyday items have seaweed in them."

11.text: The author wrote this article most likely to--
options: give facts about an ocean plant
tell about people who eat ocean plants
tell how to cook with ocean plants
11.explanation: The article provides factual information about seaweed, explaining what it is, where it grows, and how it is used in various everyday products.

12.text: In an Internet search about oceans, which website would most likely have information about where red seaweed grows?
options: Life in the Ocean: Learn about whales, dolphins, and many other creatures of the ocean...
Ocean Habitats: Learn to recognize the ocean homes of many types of fish...
Discover Ocean Plants: Find interesting facts about plants that live in the ocean...
Photos of the Ocean Floor: Follow a team of divers who take amazing pictures of the ocean floor...
Foods From the Ocean: Discover how food from the ocean ends up on people's plates...
12.explanation: The website "Discover Ocean Plants" would be most likely to have information about where red seaweed grows, as seaweed is a type of ocean plant.

13.text: What makes the secret message appear in "Lemony Letter"?
13.explanation: The instructions state: "Have the person who receives your message hold the paper near a light bulb. The heat will make the secret message appear!"

14.text: In "Mirror Message" when the steam in the bathroom is gone, the message will most likely--
14.explanation: The message only appears when steam covers the mirror. When the steam clears and goes away, the message would no longer be visible.

15.text: In step 3 of "Mirror Message," what does the word <u>invisible</u> mean?
15.explanation: In this context, "invisible" means the message cannot be seen or is hidden from view until the steam makes it appear.

16.text: "Lemony Letter" and "Mirror Message" are alike because both--
options: need the use of a lamp
have messages that must be dry to be read
have messages that must be painted to be read
16.explanation: Both methods require adult assistance: "Lemony Letter" needs a grownup to cut the lemon in half, and "Mirror Message" needs a grownup to peel the potato.

17.text: In "Crazy Crayon," it is hard to see the message before painting over it because the message--
options: needs to be next to light
takes a long time to change color
is written in a white color
17.explanation: The instructions say to use a white crayon on white paper, making it "difficult to see the markings" because white crayon on white paper is nearly invisible.

18.text: One reason to read the flier is to--
options: find out when spies need to use secret messages
learn how secret messages are made
discover secret messages that have been sent in the past
learn about the first person to send a secret message
18.explanation: The flier provides step-by-step instructions for three different methods of creating secret messages, teaching readers how to make them.

19.text: The author puts numbers before some sentences in the flier to--
options: list the steps in the order of importance
order the steps the reader will follow
show how many items the reader needs in each step
tell about how many minutes each step will take
19.explanation: The numbers indicate the sequential order of steps that must be followed to successfully create each type of secret message.

20.text:
Read this sentence and dictionary entry.
In the winter, grocery stores charge too much for strawberries.
charge (chärj) v. 1. To give orders. 2. To set as a price. 3. To fill up completely. 4. To rush forward.
20.explanation: In the context of grocery stores charging "too much" for strawberries, "charge" means "to set as a price," which is definition 2.

21.text:
Guide words:
camera - cause

Which two words would appear on the same page as these guide words?
21.explanation: Guide words show the first and last entries on a dictionary page. "Carrot" and "canal" fall alphabetically between "camera" and "cause." "Cabin" comes before "camera" and "cave" comes after "cause."

22.text: The title tells readers that a character in the story will most likely--
22.explanation: The title "A Hidden Treasure" suggests that characters will be looking for or searching for something that is hidden.

23.text: Paragraph 5 is important to the story because it--
options: tells what is on the map
tells why Evan likes to go fishing
23.explanation: Paragraph 5 describes what Evan found on the map: "Grandma's house, a raindrop inside a square, two little triangles, and a dock" with an "X" marking the "Greatest Fishing Spot."

24.text: After Evan and Mark find the map, they both feel--
24.explanation: The text shows their excitement: Evan asks "Excitedly" if they can find the fishing spot, Mark says "Let's try," and "they thundered down the steps," showing they are eager to start their search.

25.text: Where does this story begin and end?
25.explanation: The story begins with Grandma painting her kitchen, and ends with the boys rushing back "into the kitchen" with their question about the dock, then planning to get fishing poles.

26.text: Based on the story, where does the map first lead the boys?
26.explanation: Mark says "The square with the raindrop is behind Grandma's house" and they look for the water tower with the faded raindrop symbol first.

27.text: Which question is answered at the end of the story?
options: What brings fish to a certain area?
What happened to the old dock?
How often did Mom go to the old dock?
How many fish does Grandma catch?
27.explanation: When the boys ask about the dock, Grandma explains: "That dock was torn down a long time ago."

28.text: Place these words in alphabetical order.
28.explanation: In alphabetical order: searched, shouted, smiled, spend, steps.

29.text: Based on paragraph 4, the reader can tell that-
options: chicks learn to eat by watching older ostriches
ostriches need people to feed them a healthy diet
plants are easier for ostriches to feed on than insects
chicks wait to eat until the grown ostriches finish
29.explanation: Paragraph 4 directly states: "The young birds learn to peck the ground and eat plants by watching older ostriches."

30.text: Paragraph 6 explains that one way ostriches keep themselves safe is by--
30.explanation: Paragraph 6 states: "Their strong legs can deliver a kick that stops a lion!"

31.text: What information can be learned by reading the chart at the end of the article?
options: What do ostriches use to build a nest?
Why do ostriches keep the herd size low?
How many eggs do ostriches lay?
31.explanation: The "Ostrich Facts" chart shows "Life span: 30-40 years," which answers how long ostriches live.

32.text: Based on the article, one way the male leader is like the females in the herd is that he helps--
32.explanation: The text states: "The male and one of the females take turns guarding and sitting on the eggs."

33.text: The feathers of an ostrich help the bird--
33.explanation: The passage explains: "Their new fluffy feathers trap air and keep the chicks warm at night."

34.text: Based on the article, what can the reader most likely tell about ostriches?
options: They can run faster than any other animal.
Their wings are their most useful part.
34.explanation: The article states: "With such speed, ostriches outrun most predators" and that they can run 43 miles per hour, showing their speed helps them escape danger.

35.text: After looking at the title, the reader knows that this poem is about--
35.explanation: The title "The Search" indicates the poem will be about someone searching or looking for something.

36.text: What does <u>pause</u> mean in line 13?
36.explanation: "Pause" means to stop briefly or for a short time. The speaker stops in their tracks when Dad asks questions.

37.text: In lines 17-20, the speaker can best be described as--
37.explanation: Lines 17-20 show disappointment and sadness: "It's surely gone missing / There's clearly no hope. / I have to give up / Find somewhere to mope." The speaker feels upset about losing the shoe.

38.text: Where is the first place the speaker looks for the shoe?
38.explanation: The first line of the poem states: "I've emptied my sports bag," which shows this was the first place searched.

39.text: Based on the events in the poem, the shoe was most likely last worn--
39.explanation: Dad asks "When was your last game?" which suggests the shoe was worn during a sports game, and the speaker empties a sports bag looking for it.

40.text: Which question is answered in the poem?
options: What is the dog's new chew toy?
Why is the dog playing outside?
What sport does the speaker play?
When was the speaker's last game?
40.explanation: The poem reveals that Otis the dog has a "new chew / With laces and treads" which turns out to be the missing shoe.

1.text: Which question is answered in paragraph 5?
options: What had Ben and Eli planned for the summer?
Where is Eli after the last week of school?
Who helps Ben solve his problem?
Where do Ben and Eli go to school?
1.explanation: Paragraph 5 states that "Eli was at his cousin's house," answering where he went after school ended.

2.text: Based on paragraph 6, Ben's mother may best be described as--
2.explanation: Ben's mother notices that he is sulking and unhappy, so she suggests an activity to help him feel better. This shows she cares about his feelings.

3.text:
A student asks this question after reading the story.
What activity to ben and Mark choose first?
Which paragraph answers this question?
3.explanation: Paragraph 9 explicitly states that Ben "decided that fishing would be a good activity to try first."

4.text: Eli shows he wants to be Mark's friend by --
options: suggesting that Mark be invited to the lake
saying that he and Mark have many things in common
asking to join Mark and Ben at summer camp next year
asking Mark and Ben to join him when he visits his cousin
4.explanation: At the end of the story, Eli suggests they go to the lake and says, "we can invite Mark to go along," showing he wants to include Ben's new friend.

5.text: Ben agrees to go to camp because he--
options: wants to make his mom happy
wants to meet new people from his school
thinks he will enjoy being outdoors
5.explanation: In paragraph 7, the text says, "Being outside did sound like a good idea," which convinces Ben to give the camp a try.

6.text: Which sentence best supports the idea that Ben is excited about summer vacation at the beginning of the story?
options: He talks to his mother about going to a summer camp.
He speaks to a friend about going to a nearby pond.
He decides that he would like to go hiking.
He mentions the length of time left in the school year.
6.explanation: In paragraph 2, Ben yells, "One more week until summer vacation!" counting down the time shows his excitement.

7.text: Once summer is over, the three boys will most likely--
options: look for other day camps in their area
play together during the school year
make more friends at their school
7.explanation: Since the story mentions Mark attends the same school as Ben, and all three are now friends, they will likely continue to play together when school starts.

8.text:
Read this sentence from paragraph 2.
Mud kept the houses cool from the soaring temperatures.
Which word has the same meaning as soaring in this sentence?
8.explanation: In the context of temperature, "soaring" means going up very high, or rising.

9.text: Which question is answered in the section titled "Clothing and Hair"?
options: How were the hairstyles of Egyptian men and women alike?
What was the most popular style of clothing for Egyptian boys and girls?
How often did Egyptians have to shave their heads?
What type of tunic was worn during special Egyptian celebrations?
9.explanation: Paragraph 5 explains that both men and women kept their hair very short or shaved their heads to stay cool.

10.text: What is the main idea of paragraph 6?
options: The Egyptians fished from the surrounding seas and the Nile River.
The Egyptians ate many types of foods from their region.
Different crops grew well in the hot climate of Egypt.
Fruits and vegetables were a favorite food for people in Egypt.
10.explanation: Paragraph 6 lists various items in the Egyptian diet, including grains, fruits, vegetables, and fish, supporting the idea that they ate many types of food.

11.text: Which of these best describes the roof of an ancient Egyptian home?
options: It was white to reflect the sun.
It was used for many purposes.
It was made from expensive materials.
11.explanation: Paragraph 3 states that people spent time on roofs for storage, family gatherings, and sleeping, meaning it had multiple purposes.

12.text: Information from the article shows that the ancient Egyptians were--
12.explanation: The Egyptians found smart ways to build cool houses, dress for the heat, and use available food, showing they were clever at adapting to their environment.

13.text: Which sentence about this article is a fact?
options: Egyptian homes took a long time to build.
The Egyptians ate foods such as beans and cucumbers.
Egyptian clothing was easy to make.
The Egyptians developed the greatest culture in history.
13.explanation: The text specifically lists beans and cucumbers as foods they ate. This is a verifiable fact from the reading.

14.text:
A student makes these notes about the article.

Which of these belongs on the blank line?
options: Stayed indoors most of the day
14.explanation: Under the "Mud Houses" section, the text notes that small windows were used to keep heat out, which fits the chart about adapting to the environment.

15.text: Which sentence is most likely true about the ancient Egyptians?
options: They avoided work that was difficult.
They liked food from distant countries.
15.explanation: The text describes a diet consisting of grains, fruits, vegetables, and fish, which are all healthy, natural foods.

16.text:
Read this sentence from the flier.
Teddy bears, posters, games, stickers, and pencils are just some of the prizes for the lucky winners.
In which word does -y mean the same as it does in lucky?
16.explanation: "Lucky" means "having luck." Similarly, "thirsty" means "having thirst." In both cases, the suffix -y turns a noun into an adjective.

17.text: Complete this list of school fair activities.
17.explanation: The section "Celebrate at the School Fair" lists three main activities: the slide, the dunking booth, and "exciting games."

18.text: Money earned during the fundraisers will be used to pay for--
18.explanation: The first paragraph states, "Help make these exciting experiences possible," referring to the spring field trips mentioned in the previous sentence.

19.text: The principal will sit in the dunking booth most likely because he wants to--
19.explanation: The dunking booth is a fundraiser activity. By sitting in the booth, the principal encourages students to buy tickets for a chance to dunk him.

20.text: What is the main reason the author wrote the flier?
options: To offer ways that students can earn money after school
To persuade students to send in recipes for a school cookbook
To amuse students with some ideas for a school fair
To tell students about future school events
20.explanation: The flier lists upcoming fundraisers (cookbook, raffle, and fair) to inform students and encourage them to participate.

21.text: Which sentence about the flier is an opinion?
options: The recipes will be enjoyed by many people.
The raffle winners will receive prizes.
The cookbooks will be sold at a later date.
The school fair will have a new activity.
The raffle tickets will be sold at the front office.
21.explanation: Stating that families will "surely enjoy" the recipes is a prediction or feeling, not a proven fact like the prices, dates, or locations.

22.text:
Read this sentence.
The factory will manufacture new tractors and other farm machines.
In this sentence, the word manufacture means--
22.explanation: To "manufacture" means to make or build something, usually in large amounts in a factory.

23.text: In which sentence is the underlined word used correctly?
options: My new shirt has <u>for</u> large buttons.
The rusted hinges make this door <u>creek</u>.
She tied a cloth belt around her <u>waste</u>.
This is the <u>main</u> street in our town.
23.explanation: "Main" means the most important. The other options use incorrect homophones: "for" should be "four," "creek" should be "creak" (sound), and "waste" should be "waist" (body).

24.text:
Select the meaning of rich as used in this sentence.
I could barely finish my slice of that rich chocolate cake.
24.explanation: When describing food like chocolate cake, "rich" means having a strong, full, and heavy flavor.

25.text:
Read paragraph 7.
"You won again," Sidney muttered, and his head drooped.
Which sentence tells why Sidney is acting this way?
options: Sidney plans to have another contest.
Sidney begins to fear for his safety.
Max keeps his pride hidden from Sidney.
Max beats Sidney in a somersault contest.
25.explanation: Sidney is sad because he lost the contest; paragraph 6 says Sidney tumbled three times, but Max did four somersaults.

26.text:
Read these sentences from paragraph 18.
"No, no," argued Alligator. "I was just yawning."
The author includes this information to show that Alligator is--
26.explanation: The alligator had just tried to snap her jaws to eat Sidney, so saying she was "yawning" is a lie to trick them.

27.text: Which sentence about the story best shows that Max is careful?
options: Max tells Sidney that one of the tricks is too dangerous.
Max admits to Sidney that he practices the tricks.
Max holds Sidney to keep him from falling off the branch.
Max speaks quietly to Sidney after winning many contests.
27.explanation: In paragraph 10, Max looks at the skinny branch and the alligator's teeth and refuses to do the trick because it is "too dangerous."

28.text: Complete this web with the most appropriate option for the blank circle.
28.explanation: The web lists "Alligator's Tricks." The alligator asked them to do somersaults, cartwheels, and walk across a skinny branch.

29.text: Which lesson does Sidney leam in the story?
options: Friendship is more important than winning.
Practicing can lead to winning contests.
Tricks should only be done in calm weather.
Being friendly means saying kind words.
29.explanation: After Max saves Sidney, Sidney realizes he was so busy trying to win he wasn't careful. He ends up glad to have a friend like Max, realizing friendship matters more than being first.

30.text: Which detail about the setting is most important to the story?
options: A tree branch hangs above a river.
The weather stays warm in the jungle.
The force of the wind can be very strong.
30.explanation: The branch hanging over the river is the most important setting detail because it places the monkeys directly above the dangerous alligator.

31.text: Based on lines 1-4 of the poem, which sentence is correct?
options: The thieves are having trouble seeing.
The thieves are stealing silver objects.
The light of the moon is shining on the thieves.
The noise outside is making the thieves nervous.
31.explanation: The poem says their "silver fur in silver light" winked at the moon, which implies the moonlight is shining on them.

32.text: The author includes lines 7 and 8 to--
options: show that the thieves are animals
explain why the thieves are quiet
describe the feelings of the characters
give reasons the young are behind the leader
32.explanation: By mentioning the "young" trailing behind and their "bushy tails," the author reveals that these "thieves" are actually animals (raccoons).

33.text: Which of these are the thieves trying to find?
33.explanation: The last stanza states they came "to snack on my dog's kibble," meaning they were looking for food.

34.text: What is the speaker doing in the poem?
34.explanation: The speaker says "I puzzled at them through the glass," meaning they are inside looking out a window.

35.text: In paragraph 3, what does <u>crushed</u> mean?
35.explanation: The text says they "crushed the popcorn into a type of flour." To make flour, you must grind something into powder, so "crushed" means ground.

36.text: Which choice best completes this cause-and-effect chart?
36.explanation: The chart describes the process of popping corn. After the pressure builds up inside the sealed kernel, the final effect is that the kernel explodes.

37.text: Which sentence about the article is an opinion?
options: Popcorn is a snack that has a long history.
Popcorn kernels contain a tiny amount of water.
Popcorn is a snack that is easy to make at home.
Popcorn continues to be sold at movie theaters.
37.explanation: Saying something is "easy" is a personal judgment or opinion. The other statements are facts about history or science.

38.text: Complete these notes.
options: People sell popcorn on the streets from wagons.
People make popcorn in microwave ovens.
People have popcorn poppers in their homes.
People add popcorn to many other types of food.
People bake bread made from popcorn flour.
38.explanation: The notes likely list ways popcorn is made or sold. The article mentions that after microwave ovens were invented, popcorn became easy to make at home.

39.text: The main reason the author wrote this article is to--
options: suggest unusual ways to make popcorn
persuade readers to eat more popcorn
list differences between types of popcorn
tell readers about the history of popcorn
39.explanation: The article explains the history of popcorn, from ancient times and American Indians to movie theaters and modern microwaves.

40.text: Which two words are synonyms?
40.explanation: "Delicious" and "tasty" are synonyms because they both describe food that has a very good flavor.

1.text: The details in paragraphs 6-8 show--
options: how many hours the cleanup will take
the feelings Tamara has about the project
1.explanation: These paragraphs reveal Callie's dilemma: Tamara invites her to Fun World on the same day she promised to help Mrs. Baker clean the lot.

2.text: Paragraphs 11-14 show that Callie's mother--
options: thinks Mrs. Baker is an excellent neighbor
agrees that the girls should go to Fun World
believes Callie can solve her own problems
knows that neighborhood gardens are useful
2.explanation: Callie's mother says "You need to make your own decisions, but I know you will do what is best," showing she trusts Callie to handle the situation herself.

3.text: Paragraph 15 is mostly about the way Callie--
options: refuses to speak to her friend at school
spends an evening talking to her mother
knows she will enjoy going to Fun World
struggles with her promise to her neighbor
3.explanation: The paragraph describes Callie thinking about her decision all evening, wanting to go to Fun World but deciding her promise to Mrs. Baker was more important.

4.text: Why does Mrs. Baker need Callie's help?
options: The neighbors do not have time to clean the lot.
The neighborhood wants to start a garden in an empty lot filled with trash.
The other children will not help because Fun World is opening.
The city is asking people to clear the empty lots near their homes.
4.explanation: Paragraph 2 explains that the empty lot is "covered with trash" and "The city is letting us use the lot for a community garden."

5.text: Which heading would be best for paragraph 2?
5.explanation: Paragraph 2 explains how the Ice Hotel is different from regular hotels because it's made entirely of ice, yet still functions like a typical hotel.

6.text:
Read this dictionary entry.
support (sə-pôrt') v. 1. To give help. 2. To hold up. 3. To keep strong. 4. To provide for.
Which meaning of support is used in paragraph 4?
6.explanation: The text says "Ice pillars support the roof," meaning the pillars hold up the roof, which matches definition 2.

7.text: The author includes paragraphs 5 and 6 most likely to--
options: describe how guests can be comfortable at the Ice Hotel
persuade people to visit the Ice Hotel
tell who would enjoy the Ice Hotel
show that new services are offered at the Ice Hotel
7.explanation: These paragraphs explain how guests stay warm with sleeping bags and can use the sauna, showing how the hotel makes cold conditions comfortable.

8.text: Which sentence about the Ice Hotel is an opinion?
options: Guests can have meals brought to their rooms.
The temperature inside is often below freezing.
Artists change the appearance of the Ice Hotel.
Building the Ice Hotel is worth the hard work.
8.explanation: Saying something is "worth it" is an opinion because it expresses a personal judgment, while the other choices are facts that can be proven.

9.text: Which detail about the hotel most likely attracts visitors' attention?
options: The workers are friendly and welcoming.
The inside of the hotel sparkles and shines.
The walls are four feet thick.
9.explanation: Paragraph 4 describes how "almost every inch sparkles like a diamond" and the hotel "gleams," which would be most eye-catching to visitors.

10.text: Branch Rickey wanted Jackie to be part of the Brooklyn Dodgers because--
options: more Americans were becoming fans of Jackie
he knew the players on the team respected Jackie
he wanted Jackie to help make the team better
Jackie was planning to leave the Negro Leagues
10.explanation: Paragraph 4 states "Branch knew that Jackie was talented enough to be part of this team," showing he wanted Jackie's talent to improve the Dodgers.

11.text: The author wrote this article most likely to--
options: compare modern sports with those Jackie Robinson played as a child
tell how Jackie Robinson played a role in the history of baseball
describe how Jackie Robinson helped the Brooklyn Dodgers
explain how Jackie Robinson became a member of the Brooklyn Dodgers
11.explanation: The article focuses on Jackie Robinson being the first African American in Major League Baseball and how this changed sports history.

12.text: Based on lines 1-4 of the poem, which sentence is correct?
options: The thieves are having trouble seeing.
The thieves are stealing silver objects.
The light of the moon is shining on the thieves.
The noise outside is making the thieves nervous.
12.explanation: Line 2 says "Their silver fur in silver light," showing the moonlight is shining on the animals' fur.

13.text: Lines 5-8 are important to the poem because they reveal--
13.explanation: These lines describe "a mask of black around her eyes" and "a mask and bushy tail," revealing the "thieves" are raccoons.

14.text: The thieves are out at night because they are--
14.explanation: Lines 15-16 reveal they "come to snack on my dog's kibble-- / To satisfy a midnight nibble!"

15.text: What is the speaker doing in the poem?
15.explanation: Line 10 says "I puzzled at them through the glass," showing the speaker is watching the raccoons through a window from inside.

16.text: The author includes the first paragraph in order to--
options: list activities people like the most
explain why the area is large
describe the many bodies of water
16.explanation: The first paragraph describes the size (500,000 acres), features (peaks, lakes, rivers), and activities available at Thatcher National Wilderness Area.

17.text:
Read this paragraph from the introduction.
Visitors are cautioned to pay attention to the surroundings while in these areas. This is a wild place with unpredictable weather changes. With miles of woods and few roads, rescue is difficult or impossible. All visitors are responsible for exploring the area safely.
What does cautioned mean?
17.explanation: The paragraph warns visitors about dangers like unpredictable weather and difficult rescue, so "cautioned" means given a warning.

18.text:
Read this thesaurus entry.
complete adj. - entire, finished, perfect, total.
Which word best replaces complete in the "Hiking Essentials" section?
18.explanation: The text refers to bringing a "complete first-aid kit," meaning one with all necessary items, so "entire" fits best.

19.text: Based on the information in the "Keep an Eye to the Sky" section, the reader can tell that the weather--
options: can change suddenly during any season
is calm during much of fall and winter
can best be enjoyed during warmer months
19.explanation: The section warns that weather "can change rapidly" and describes sudden thunderstorms in summer and unexpected snowstorms in fall.

20.text: In which section would the author most likely add information about planning when to hike?
20.explanation: "Set a Turnaround Time" already discusses planning when to turn back and timing hikes, making it the logical place for when to hike.

21.text: The flier shows that Thatcher National Wilderness Area has all of these EXCEPT--
options: weather that allows for many outdoor activities
staff who take hikers up the mountains
areas that present safety problems for visitors
hiking trails that contribute to its popularity
21.explanation: The flier emphasizes visitor responsibility and self-reliance, never mentioning staff guides taking hikers up mountains.

22.text: Which sentence is the best summary of the flier?
options: Visitors who take the time to prepare will enjoy the activities in Thatcher National Wilderness Area.
Hikers must pack the right type of gear for the trails in Thatcher National Wilderness Area.
Visitors should dress warmly for hiking in the mountains of Thatcher National Wilderness Area.
Hikers can fish and camp in certain areas around the lakes and streams of Thatcher National Wilderness Area.
22.explanation: The flier emphasizes preparation and safety measures throughout, ending with "With preparation and a few safety measures, visitors will find that TNWA offers endless and rewarding experiences."

23.text: The author includes information about the setting in paragraph 1 to--
options: tell why there is a school in the story
describe the weather on the prairie
help the reader understand the time period of the story
show that the house is beside a creek
23.explanation: The one-room schoolhouse and prairie setting help establish this as a historical story taking place in the past.

24.text: Why does the author include paragraph 4?
options: To show how Benjamin felt riding in a wagon
To show that Benjamin's family took a long trip
To explain why Benjamin's family moved
To explain why Benjamin had few books
24.explanation: The paragraph explains that the wagon had limited space for necessities, so Benjamin could only bring two books, explaining his book shortage.

25.text: What is paragraph 13 mainly about?
options: Benjamin is anxious when he reads the letter Mr. Peters sends.
Benjamin goes to the general store with Papa and looks for a letter in the mail.
Benjamin waits for weeks to receive a letter because of the long distance.
Benjamin hopes to receive a letter and is delighted once it arrives with good news.
25.explanation: The paragraph describes Benjamin checking for mail over several weeks, then shouting with delight when Mr. Peters' letter finally arrives saying the book wagon will come.

26.text: Why does Papa tell Benjamin that he can pack two books on the wagon?
options: The trip is too short to read more than a couple of books.
The family has a small space to fit the books.
Benjamin is encouraged to bring books for his sister.
Papa will buy books when they arrive at their new home.
26.explanation: Paragraph 4 explains "Most of the space in their horse-drawn wagon was taken up by necessities," leaving little room for books.

27.text: Benjamin begins thinking of faraway places when he--
options: hears about a library that is in another town
sees himself as a character in a story he is reading
notices a book in the schoolhouse after school
decides to write a letter asking about a book wagon
27.explanation: Paragraph 3 describes how when reading King Arthur, "Benjamin was a brave king leading his loyal knights," showing he imagines himself in the story.

28.text: What is the main conflict of the story?
options: Benjamin wants to read a book during the summer.
Papa will not allow Benjamin to take more books to Kansas.
Benjamin is looking for more adventure books to read.
Miss Cotter does not own the book that Benjamin wants.
28.explanation: The main problem is that Benjamin wants books to read during summer but the library books must be returned and the nearest library is too far away.

29.text: What is the most important reason Miss Cotter tells Benjamin about Mr. Peters?
options: She must return the books Benjamin wants to read.
She wonders if Benjamin has been to the library.
She thinks Benjamin could help him start a book wagon.
She wants Benjamin to wait for him to arrive.
29.explanation: Miss Cotter mentions the book wagon because she has to return the library books Benjamin wants to borrow, offering the book wagon as an alternative.

30.text: After Benjamin reads the letter, he most likely feels--
options: amazed that Mr. Peters sent a reply
thrilled that the book wagon is coming to his town
honored that Mr. Peters is coming to visit him
relieved that the wagon has many books
30.explanation: Benjamin "shouted with delight" when he read that Mr. Peters is bringing the book wagon, showing he's thrilled about this news.

31.text: Which word is a synonym for <u>settle</u> as it is used in paragraph 1?
31.explanation: The passengers "planned to settle in new frontier towns," meaning they planned to live there permanently.

32.text: What does <u>jolt</u> mean in paragraph 2?
32.explanation: The ship "shook with a tremendous jolt" when it hit the tree, indicating a sudden, jarring movement.

33.text: Which question is answered in the "Searching for a Buried Treasure" section of the article?
options: How long did it take David Hawley to find the Arabia?
Why did David Hawley look for the Arabia somewhere other than in the Missouri River?
In what year did David Hawley find out about the Arabia?
What city did David Hawley travel to in order to gather information about the Arabia?
33.explanation: Paragraph 5 explains that the Missouri River's path had changed over the years, so the Arabia was now in a farmer's field, not in the river.

34.text: Paragraph 11 helps the reader to understand that the pioneers--
options: planned to move into cabins already built for them
were fearful of the hard life ahead of them
knew supplies would be hard to find where they were going
34.explanation: The paragraph lists many supplies the pioneers brought, from food to building materials, suggesting they knew these items wouldn't be available at their destination.

35.text: Which sentence best states the main idea of paragraph 14?
options: The history of the Arabia has been preserved in a museum.
People want to see the many treasures that were once part of the Arabia.
Hawley wanted people to know about the pioneers on the Arabia.
Treasures from the Arabia are worth more today than they were a century ago.
35.explanation: The paragraph explains that Hawley chose to create a museum to share the Arabia with the world, preserving its history.

36.text: According to the article, which part of the ship was uncovered first?
36.explanation: Paragraph 8 states "It was part of the Arabia's paddle wheel!" as the first piece of the ship they found.

37.text: In which word does -<u>al</u> have the same meaning as it does in sign<u>al</u>?
37.explanation: In "signal" and "natural," the suffix "-al" means "relating to" or "having the nature of."

38.text: According to the article, the objects that were discovered showed--
options: what the lives of the pioneers on the steamboat were like
that steamboats could carry a large amount of cargo
where the people on the steamboat came from
that there was enough food for everyone on the steamboat
38.explanation: Paragraphs 9-11 explain how the recovered supplies "offered a rare history lesson" showing "how the pioneers lived."

39.text: The accident most likely happened because the--
options: captain was inside the pilot house
cargo on the boat was too heavy
captain was unable to see under the water
39.explanation: Paragraph 2 says the ship hit "a fallen tree hidden beneath the river's surface," meaning they couldn't see it underwater.

40.text: Which sentence did the author include in the article to suggest that the project was expensive?
options: He wondered whether it might be possible to find the ship.
Curious, he went to libraries and gathered information.
Recovering the steamboat was a massive task.
Hawley's brother, father, and friends worked with him.
40.explanation: Calling it a "massive task" that required hiring companies with heavy equipment suggests the project was large and expensive.

41.text: The author most likely wrote the article to--
options: explain how people lived in the past
create a story about a shipwreck
tell about an early form of transportation
describe a discovery from the past
41.explanation: The article focuses on David Hawley's discovery and recovery of the Arabia steamboat and its historical treasures.

42.text: The article supports the idea that--
options: David Hawley did most of the work to recover the ship
the Arabia was the largest steamboat of its time
David Hawley enjoys hunting for lost treasures
the Arabia was the first shipwreck to be dug out of river mud
42.explanation: The article describes Hawley as a "treasure hunter" who researched and pursued finding the Arabia, suggesting he enjoys this type of work.

1.text: What does the word <u>devised</u> mean in paragraph 2?
1.explanation: The context mentions Mrs. Barnes had "devised the plan," and she asks "What do you mean?" implying she originated or created the idea.

2.text: At the beginning of the story, what does Charlie think about the morning news program?
options: He feels it lacks a fun ending.
He expects it to include the lunch menu.
He believes it needs more order.
He wants it to contain music.
